New Azure SQL databases have Query Store {{c1::enabled by default}}.
column2:
New Azure SQL databases start collecting Query Store information by default. New SQL Server databases also enable it in READ_WRITE mode starting with SQL Server 2022. Existing databases can retain different settings.
Review source

column1: To force plan 17 for query 42, run {{c1::EXEC sys.sp_query_store_force_plan @query_id = 42, @plan_id = 17;}}
column2:
query_id selects the captured statement and plan_id selects a plan belonging to it. The procedure asks the optimizer to use that plan. It does not guarantee success on every future compilation.
Review source

column1: To stop forcing plan 17 for query 42, run {{c1::EXEC sys.sp_query_store_unforce_plan @query_id = 42, @plan_id = 17;}}
column2:
Unforcing removes the request to use plan 17 for query 42. The optimizer is free to select a plan again. This action does not delete the plan or its recorded history.
Review source

column1: On a platform that supports Query Store hints, apply MAXDOP 1 to query 42 with {{c1::EXEC sys.sp_query_store_set_hints @query_id = 42, @query_hints = N'OPTION (MAXDOP 1)';}}
column2:
MAXDOP 1 requests a serial plan for this query without editing the application statement. The hint is associated with query 42 in the current database, not with every query that runs there.
Review source

column1: Remove Query Store hints from query 42 with {{c1::EXEC sys.sp_query_store_clear_hints @query_id = 42;}}
column2:
Clearing hints removes the Query Store tuning instructions for this query ID. It does not erase captured plans or runtime measurements, so you can still compare performance before and after the change.
Review source

column1: In Azure SQL Database, enable Query Store wait collection with {{c1::ALTER DATABASE CURRENT SET QUERY_STORE (WAIT_STATS_CAPTURE_MODE = ON);}}
column2:
Wait collection adds historical wait categories for captured queries and plans. These measurements help separate delays such as lock waits from query work, rather than only telling you that the query was slow.
Review source

column1: Query Store's query text is available in {{c1::sys.query_store_query_text}}.
column2:
This view stores the statement text. Join on query_text_id to sys.query_store_query to connect that text to its query ID and the metadata used to find its plans.
Review source

column1: Query Store's execution counts and aggregate durations are available in {{c1::sys.query_store_runtime_stats}}.
column2:
These statistics summarize executions by plan and interval. Join on plan_id to identify the plan, then on query_id to find its statement. The count describes represented runs, not a row per run.
Review source

column1: The avg_duration column in sys.query_store_runtime_stats uses {{c1::microseconds}}.
column2:
This catalog value uses microseconds, so 25,000 means 25 milliseconds. Convert the unit before comparing it with application timings expressed in milliseconds.
Review source

column1: Inspect plan-forcing failures in {{c1::sys.query_store_plan}} using force_failure_count and last_force_failure_reason_desc.
column2:
A forcing flag shows the request to use the plan, not that every attempt succeeded. A rising failure count or a recorded failure reason tells you to investigate rather than trust the flag alone.
Review source

column1: When Query Store switches to {{c1::READ_ONLY}}, it stops collecting new query data.
column2:
In READ_ONLY mode, Query Store still lets you read its existing history but does not collect new query data. Inspect the reason if the mode changed unexpectedly.
Review source

column1: In Azure SQL Database, raise Query Store's quota to 1,024 MB with {{c1::ALTER DATABASE CURRENT SET QUERY_STORE (MAX_STORAGE_SIZE_MB = 1024);}}
column2:
The option sets the Query Store quota in megabytes, not the database's maximum size. A larger quota gives retained history more room, but it does not change which queries the capture policy selects.
Review source

column1: In Azure SQL Database Query Performance Insight, the line shows overall database {{c1::DTU percentage}}, while bars show selected queries' CPU use.
column2:
Query Performance Insight shows database transaction unit (DTU) use for the whole database. Its line uses the maximum within each hour, whereas the bars represent CPU for selected queries.
Review source

column1: QPI's Custom tab can rank queries by CPU, duration, or {{c1::execution count}}.
column2:
Rank by execution count to find queries that run most often, even if each run is cheap. Rank by CPU or duration when frequency is not the main symptom.
Review source

column1: QPI chart annotations show recommendations from {{c1::Database Advisor}}.
column2:
An annotation is a marker for a recommendation displayed on the performance timeline. Open the marker to read the recommendation and consider it alongside the query measurements.
Review source
